summary: iNiS and Nintendo's stylus-driven DS rhythm trilogy: the Japan-exclusive Ouendan games plus the Western counterpart Elite Beat Agents.

entries.title: Osu! Tatakae! Ouendan

emulation.notes: Useful for capture, but stylus timing and two-screen layout are most authentic on DS hardware.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: DS-resolution 2D presentation; emulator scaling helps capture but does not replace original touch input.

primary.why: Ouendan was released only for Nintendo DS, and its stylus/touchscreen timing is central to the game, so the original DS release is the complete primary route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the original Nintendo DS cartridge on DS hardware for authentic touch input. Use melonDS or DeSmuME only when capture convenience outweighs original touchscreen feel.

all_releases.fidelity: Original DS dual-screen, stylus-driven rhythm release.
all_releases.reason: primary: only official platform and complete original release.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: There is no official remaster or higher-fidelity port; original DS hardware is the authentic complete route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official remaster or port is documented.

entries.title: Elite Beat Agents

emulation.notes: Useful for capture, but DS hardware best preserves the touch-control feel.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: DS-resolution 2D presentation with emulator scaling for capture.

primary.why: Elite Beat Agents was released for Nintendo DS and is the international counterpart to Ouendan with its own characters, scenarios, and licensed-song set; the original DS cartridge is the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the original Nintendo DS cartridge on DS hardware for authentic touch input. Use melonDS or DeSmuME only for capture/upscaling convenience.

all_releases.fidelity: Original DS dual-screen, stylus-driven rhythm release.
all_releases.reason: primary: only official platform and complete original release.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: There is no official remaster or alternate platform release.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official remaster or port is documented.

entries.title: Moero! Nekketsu Rhythm Damashii: Osu! Tatakae! Ouendan 2

emulation.notes: Useful for capture, but original DS hardware best preserves the stylus timing and wireless-play context.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: DS-resolution 2D presentation with emulator scaling for capture.

primary.why: Ouendan 2 was released only for Nintendo DS, adds the sequel's rival cheer squad and four-player wireless support, and has no documented modern port.
primary.how_to_play: Play the original Nintendo DS cartridge on DS hardware for authentic stylus timing. Use melonDS or DeSmuME only for capture; note that limited-time DS Download Station character-skin content is no longer normally obtainable.

all_releases.fidelity: Original DS dual-screen, stylus-driven rhythm release.
all_releases.reason: primary: only official platform and complete cartridge release.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The cartridge is the only official release, but historical limited-time DS Download Station skins/multiplayer characters are no longer normally obtainable.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official remaster or port is documented; limited-time DS Download Station character content was separate from normal cartridge access.
